title: Comparative limits on contractual discretion and good faith
summary: The supplement’s notes compare different approaches to good faith and the review of contractual powers, including Braganza, Yam Seng, and Wastech.
notes:
These short extracts and descriptions should be read as comparative authorities with different legal settings. They ask whether a power must be exercised for its contractual purpose, whether an obligation arises by implication in the particular relationship, and how far a court may review discretionary judgment.

The notes are not full opinions. They do not establish that the jurisdictions adopt one interchangeable general rule, or that good faith always requires a party to subordinate its interests. Ng Giap’s resistance to a general implied duty remains distinct from the approaches discussed in the notes.

textbookImport.basis: Paraphrase of the actual Fall 2026 course supplement. The source retains its own date and legal context; no current-law verification.

topics.discretion: The notes compare legal limits on a contractual decision-maker’s choices.
topics.good-faith: They preserve differences between jurisdictions and sources of implication.
